verdicts.claim: VR learns from feedback (evaluate_point MAE ↓, primary signal)
verdicts.evidence: 21/24 seeds (88%) show evaluate_point MAE lower in last iteration with data than first. Additionally, 17/24 seeds show a >50% MAE reduction (first iter to last iter).

verdicts.claim: OAT direction accuracy improves over iterations (secondary; OATs are front-loaded)
verdicts.evidence: 10/13 seeds (77%) show OAT direction accuracy higher in last non-None iter than first. Note: many seeds only have 1 iteration with OAT sweeps, so this metric is noisier than eval_point MAE.
36/40 seeds (90%) show surprise count lower in last iteration than first

verdicts.claim: Prediction improvement precedes HV breakthroughs (learning → exploitation coupling)
verdicts.evidence: Only 0/18 seeds (0%) show coupling — breakthroughs happen independent of prediction improvement.

verdicts.claim: OAT-discovered input importance guides exploitation targets (model → exploitation causal link)
verdicts.evidence: Only 1/14 seeds (7%) show the expected correlation.

verdicts.claim: Exploitation targets are better than random (LHS) on maximize objectives
verdicts.evidence: 14/14 seeds (100%) have exploitation targets with higher mean Y1 or Y4 than LHS. 14/14 are better on BOTH.

verdicts.claim: Exploration (OAT) is more surprising than exploitation (evaluate_point)
verdicts.evidence: OAT surprise rate (iter 0) = 75% vs evaluate_point surprise rate (first exploit iter) = 58%. Agent encounters more surprises when probing new territory than when using its model, consistent with the model providing useful guidance.

verdicts.claim: Exploitation surprise rate decreases over iterations (model improves during exploitation)
Better prediction accuracy predicts higher HV
verdicts.evidence: Pooled Pearson r=-0.038, p=0.826, n=36. Weak or near-zero correlation — may be driven by within-condition noise or between-condition mixing.
